Plot a LinDA Result

Source: R/linda.r
plot.ecodive_linda.Rd

Views of a linda() result for one covariate, each feature a point (or a row), with the features declared differentially abundant (reject = TRUE) highlighted and the most significant of them named:

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ecodive_linda'
plot(
  x,
  covariate = NULL,
  type = c("volcano", "effect", "ma", "forest"),
  labels = 10,
  n_features = 30,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

The result of linda().

covariate

Which covariate's log2 fold changes to plot, as named in the result's covariate column (such as "statusmoderate" or "age"). Defaults to the first column of the term of interest (groups), or else to the first covariate.

type

The plot: "volcano" (the default), "effect", "ma", or "forest".

labels

How many of the differentially abundant features to name (in the volcano, effect and MA plots), those with the smallest adjusted p-values. Default 10; 0 for none.

n_features

For "forest": how many features to show, those with the smallest adjusted p-values (ties in the table's order). Default 30; Inf for all.

conf_level

For "forest": the confidence level of the intervals. Default 0.95.

...

Passed on to graphics::plot.default(), such as main, sub, xlab, xlim or cex.

Value

x, invisibly.

Details

  • "volcano" (the default): the log2 fold change against the adjusted p-value.

  • "effect": the log2 fold change against the residual standard deviation (for a two-level comparison).

  • "ma": the log2 fold change against the mean clr abundance.

  • "forest": the log2 fold changes and their confidence intervals of the n_features most significant features.

Log fold changes are in log2, as LinDA estimates them (the result's log_base), bias-corrected.

  • Volcano plot. The y axis is \(-\log_{10}\) of p_adjusted (an adjusted p-value of 0 is drawn at the smallest positive double), with a dashed line at alpha.

  • Effect plot. The x axis is the feature's residual standard deviation (the resid_sd attribute, log2); the dashed lines are \(y = \pm x\). Only for a covariate whose design column is 0 or 1 (a factor's level against its reference).

  • MA plot. The x axis is the feature's mean centred log2 ratio (the mean attribute).

  • Forest plot. Bars over \(\mathrm{log2\_fc} \pm q\,\mathrm{se}\), with \(q\) the \((1 + \)conf_level\()/2\) quantile of the t distribution with dof degrees of freedom, as the p-values; they aren't adjusted for testing many features.

Features whose values are NaN are left out. The subtitle names the covariate and counts the features rejected.

Examples

    set.seed(1)
    x <- matrix(rpois(20 * 30, 40), 20, 30)
    x[11:20, 1:3] <- x[11:20, 1:3] * 5
    res <- linda(x, groups = rep(c('a', 'b'), each = 10))
    plot(res)

    plot(res, type = 'effect')

    plot(res, type = 'forest', n_features = 10)
